walkthroughs.body_html:
Anglo-Saxon & Norman England c1060-88 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Anglo-Saxon & Norman England c1060-88 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Anglo-Saxon & Norman England c1060-88.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In what year was the Domesday Book completed?
What was the name of William's brutal northern campaign?
options: The Anarchy
Harrying of the North
Northern Crusade
York Suppression

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
Anglo-Saxons punished all crimes with imprisonment in castle dungeons.
William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.

mcqs.q: How was crime punished in Anglo-Saxon England?
options: Anglo-Saxons punished all crimes with imprisonment in castle dungeons.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
Through wergild ('man-price') compensation for victims, communal responsibility via tithings, trial by ordeal in disputed cases, and the death penalty for serious crimes.
Anglo-Saxons had no laws and just took revenge on each other.

mcqs.q: How did Anglo-Saxons come to dominate post-Roman Britain?
options: Anglo-Saxons invaded Britain and wiped out all the Romano-British inhabitants.
A mix of migration from northern Germany and Denmark, settlement and intermarriage, and cultural absorption of Romano-British populations — not simple invasion and replacement.
Anglo-Saxons punished all crimes with imprisonment in castle dungeons.
Anglo-Saxons came as refugees fleeing the Vikings.
